s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal mass with mild discomfort during exercise
salient_findings: Painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
Solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass on scrotal ultrasonography
key_facts: 16-year-old male with no prior medical history
Noted a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier
Denies any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
Lump's size remained unchanged over two months
Experienced mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
Painless mass on physical examination
Testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
Mass contained two small hypoechoic foci
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers were all within normal limits

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Most common epididymal tumor, matches patient's age and presentation

shortlist.label: Epididymal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign condition, could explain painless scrotal mass

shortlist.label: Spermatocele
shortlist.why_kept: Benign cystic lesion, possible cause of scrotal mass

shortlist.label: Epididymal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor, could be considered given patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Papillary cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare benign tumor, but should be considered due to patient's age and ultrasound findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic mass at the tail of the epididymis with two small hypoechoic foci, as seen on scrotal ultrasonography, is consistent with an adenomatoid tumor, which is a common benign tumor of the epididymis in young men.

rejected.label: Epididymal cyst
rejected.why: Epididymal cysts are typically fluid-filled and anechoic on ultrasound, which does not match the solid, hyperechoic mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Spermatocele
rejected.why: Spermatoceles are cystic lesions that contain sperm and are typically anechoic on ultrasound, which does not match the solid mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Epididymal lipoma
rejected.why: Epididymal lipomas are rare and would likely appear as a hyperechoic mass on ultrasound, but the presence of two small hypoechoic foci is not typical for a lipoma.

rejected.label: Papillary cystadenoma
rejected.why: Papillary cystadenomas are rare tumors that are typically associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease and would not be the most likely diagnosis in a healthy 16-year-old male with no prior medical history.
